title: Architecture work
description: The files the architecture team of one Epic hands to each other and to the script: the solutions architect's state and result, the requests it writes for the agents it starts and their answers, a reviewer's result for the unapproved content, the lead's routing, the question put to the decider and its ruling, and the comparison of what a Story built. The root is the architect's result; each other file has its own schema file that refers to its definition here. A matrix id is the id of an entry as atw-matrix prints it. The review scope a reviewer is handed is what atw-matrix review-scope prints for the Epic, narrowed to the reviewer's criteria.

NeedState.description: The architect's first judgment of one need against the effective architecture (the effective arc42 as it stands before this Epic). Effective means approved as of now, never complete or correct. `approved`: the architect judges that effective statements meet the need as they stand. `disagreement`: effective statements bear on the need and two of them disagree. `missing`: no effective statement meets the need.

StateConclusion.description: The architect's first judgment, a starting point and no result. `effective-architecture-meets-every-need`: every need is `approved`, so the architect's work starts from the questions its expertise raises about the effective architecture. `work-remains`: at least one need is `disagreement` or `missing`.

Conclusion.description: What the architect concluded. Every conclusion goes through the architecture check and the review. `no-change-needed`: the architect judged that the Epic needs nothing added, changed or removed in the approved architecture, and `criteria` cites the effective documents and headings that meet it; the review checks that judgment. `changes-designed`: the architect designed, changed, removed or settled something for the Epic. `unsettled`: at least one matter is listed in `unsettled`.

CriterionStatus.description: `satisfied`: `satisfiedAt` names where. `not-applicable`: `reason` says why the criterion does not apply to this PRD.

UnsettledKind.description: `technical-choice`: two positions remain, each with evidence and a real cost. `business-conflict`: two business requirements that no design meets together, or a design that only works against section 2.

RequestKind.description: `question`: one question to answer. `task`: one bounded piece of design, or one diagram to draw.

TrdMode.description: `draft`: write the TRD from the PRD and the approved arc42 material. `update`: apply the listed changes and nothing else.

RequirementKind.description: `obligation`: something that must be true of an element, with a checkable value. `reuse`: the element obtains a behaviour from a shared capability and does not implement its own.

Routing.description: What the lead decides for one item. `reject`: the finding goes no further. `correct`: the architect corrects it and the reviewer that raised it re-checks. `opinion`: one specialist is asked, and the answer goes to the architect with the correction. `competing-design`: the architect designs the other position of one matter. `decider`: the decider rules.

OwnerConcernKind.description: `business-conflict`: two business requirements cannot both be met by any design. `section-2-conflict`: the only workable design conflicts with a section 2 constraint.

Citation.description: Where something is stated or can be checked.

source.description: An arc42 path relative to the architecture root, a PRD or TRD path, an AWS documentation URL, code as repository, revision and file:line, or an earlier specialist's answer file.

heading.description: The heading in that document, or the id of the PRD or TRD requirement; an empty string when the source has none.

Need.description: One thing the PRD needs of the architecture, and the architect's judgment of it.

id.description: N1, N2 and so on, unique in the file.

need.description: What the PRD needs, in one sentence.

prdRequirements.description: The PRD requirement headings the need comes from.

evidence.description: The approved statements judged, and for a disagreement the statements that disagree.

judgment.description: Why the state is what it is.

ArchitectureContext.description: The context file of one Epic's architecture work. The open-run step of the elaboration writes it; every step of the architecture part is handed it, and the solutions architect's brief names it as `context`. It names every path the script chose, so that no agent and no step derives one.

architectureRoot.description: The architecture folder of the vault, which holds `arc42/`, `built/` and `reference/`.

vaultCommit.description: The vault commit the matrix's document rows are synced to.

matrixCommand.description: The command that reads and writes the matrix.

statePath.description: Where the solutions architect writes its state file.

resultPath.description: Where the solutions architect writes its result file.

trdPath.description: Where the TRD of this Epic is written and kept; every TRD request names this path.

helpersFolder.description: The folder for the request files the solutions architect writes and the answer files it names in them.

CheckResult.description: What the check step of the architecture part found before review: every defect a script can find in the matrix, in the documents it indexes and in the solutions architect's result. The script writes it; when `valid` is false the solutions architect is handed it as `findings` and corrects each problem.

valid.description: True when the check found no problem.

unansweredCriteria.description: The ids of the architecture and technical-requirement criteria the result gives no answer for.

corrections.description: How many corrections of mechanical defects came before this check.

ArchitectureState.description: The solutions architect's judgment of the state of the architecture for this PRD, written before it does anything else.

FeatureEntry.description: One feature the PRD needs, as the architect recorded it in the matrix.

id.description: The matrix id of the feature entry.

prdRequirements.description: The PRD requirement headings the feature serves.

elements.description: The matrix ids of the elements that realize it.

sharedCapabilities.description: The matrix ids of the supporting features it uses.

NoFeature.description: One PRD requirement the architect judges no feature serves, with the reason.

requirement.description: The matrix id of the requirement, or its PRD requirement heading.

reason.description: Why no feature serves it: for example, it states no behaviour of the system.

SharedUse.description: One element that obtains behaviours from a shared capability and does not implement them itself, by pointer: `atw-matrix node <capability>` returns each `provides` item with its `behaviour`, `consumersMust`, `interface`, `useSignals` and `duplicateSignals`.

element.description: The matrix id of the element that uses the capability.

capability.description: The matrix id of the supporting feature.

relies.description: The ids of the capability's `provides` items the element obtains, as the `supportedBy` relationship's `relies` records them.

FactEntry.description: One design fact with its one home.

id.description: The id of the fact, unique in the file.

statement.description: The fact, at architecture level, in the form its arc42 section requires.

home.description: The one arc42 document and heading that states the fact.

linkedFrom.description: The arc42 paths of the documents that link to the home and do not restate the fact.

CriterionAnswer.description: The architect's answer to one criterion of effective-architecture/review-criteria.json whose level is architecture or technical-requirement.

satisfiedAt.description: For `satisfied`, each arc42 document and heading, or the TRD path with a requirement id as the heading, that satisfies it; empty for `not-applicable`.

reason.description: For `not-applicable`, why the criterion does not apply to this PRD; an empty string for `satisfied`.

SpecNote.description: One detail below architecture and technical-requirement level that is already known, kept for the spec authors.

element.description: The matrix id of the element the detail concerns.

detail.description: The route, field, key, parameter, name or schema detail.

source.description: Where the detail comes from: a path and heading, a URL, or `design` for something decided in this run.

Position.description: One of the positions on a matter.

id.description: A short name for the position, unique in the matter.

UnsettledMatter.description: A matter the architect could not settle, or the question the lead puts to the decider: the matter and the positions on it.

id.description: U1, U2 and so on, unique in the file.

matter.description: What has to be decided, in one or two sentences.

Choice.description: A decision the architect made between alternatives that each had a cost.

fact.description: The matrix id of the fact that states what was chosen.

alternatives.description: The alternatives that were not chosen.

CostEvidence.description: The unit math behind one cost constraint in the TRD.

resource.description: The matrix id of the billable element.

assumptions.description: The stated usage the estimate rests on.

unitMath.description: The arithmetic, with the fixed monthly floor kept apart from usage cost.

ReviewSignals.description: The facts about this run's design that the reviewer groups of effective-architecture/review-criteria.json name in `appliesWhen.result`. A script selects reviewers from them; an empty list selects none.

failureBehaviours.description: The matrix ids of the facts this run decided that state retry, dead-letter, idempotent or recovery behaviour.

newRuntimeResources.description: The matrix ids of elements this run added that run in AWS.

newBillableResources.description: The matrix ids of elements this run added that AWS bills for and the approved design did not already hold.

changedBillableLimits.description: The TRD requirement ids whose limit or volume on an existing billable element this run changed.

newPatterns.description: The matrix ids of each new service, new shared capability, and element of a resource type the matrix had not held.

SpecialistGap.description: One question no specialist's specialty covers, or one answer that showed a specialist lacks what its specialty needs, so that the specialist is enhanced.

agent.description: The agent's name, or the specialty no agent covers.

lacked.description: What the specialist lacked, or what no specialty covers.

request.description: The path of the request file that showed it.

ArchitectureResult.description: The solutions architect's result for one Epic, at the context file's `resultPath`. The architect writes it as the work goes, so that a session that stops loses nothing: the members settled so far, written as soon as the state file is written and rewritten in place each time a part settles (a fact and its home, a settlement, a feature, a criterion answer, a note for the specs). The file satisfies this schema when the architect finishes; until then it is the partial result a `Finish` step, or a session started again, continues from. The script reads `conclusion`, checks every criterion answer, and selects reviewers from `reviewSignals`; what is unapproved comes from the matrix, not from this file. For a `no-change-needed` conclusion the reviewers are also handed the effective documents `criteria` cites. Every conclusion goes to review; none ends the architecture work by itself.

noFeature.description: Every requirement of the Epic that no feature serves. The step that accepts the result fails on a requirement that is neither served by a feature nor listed here.

addedOrChangedElements.description: The matrix ids, as recorded, of every element this design adds or changes for the Epic (services, components, infrastructure, events, routing rules, layers and packages), including every element a TRD requirement binds that this design adds or changes. The Epic's Stories build exactly these. An element the Epic only uses is not listed: it is context for the Tasks, never work. An event is built in each stack that holds one of its producers. The step that accepts the result fails on an id the matrix lacks, an entry not on the architecture side, an event with no description, and an entry built in no stack (for an event, one none of whose producers is homed in a stack).

sharedCapabilities.description: Every shared capability the design uses, as the `supportedBy` relationships the architect recorded state them.

facts.description: The design facts this run decided.

settledDisagreements.description: The matrix ids of the disagreements this run settled; what the losing statement must change goes in the write request.

criteria.description: One answer for every criterion whose level is architecture or technical-requirement. A criterion with neither a place it is satisfied nor a reason it does not apply is unfinished work.

notesForSpecs.description: Implementation-level details already known (route method and path, field, key and index names, parameter, metric and alarm names, payload schemas), kept for the spec authors.

specialistGaps.description: Each question no specialist's specialty covers, and each answer that showed a specialist lacks what its specialty needs, so the specialist is enhanced.

SpecialistRequest.description: What the solutions architect, or the lead when it asks for an opinion, asks of one design specialist or diagram author.

bounds.description: For a task, exactly what is to be decided and what is not; an empty string for a question.

concerns.description: The PRD sections and arc42 headings the request concerns, and nothing wider.

trustedCode.description: The matrix ids of the entries the matrix marks verified. Code of any other entry is a hint only.

answerPath.description: The absolute path the answer is written to, under the context file's `helpersFolder`.

NeededSpecialty.description: Another specialty the answer needs, for the architect to ask.

DesignFact.description: One decision a bounded task returns, for the architect to accept or change.

section.description: The arc42 section the fact belongs in: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 8.

Diagram.description: One diagram for architecture-maintainer to place.

home.description: The arc42 document and heading the diagram belongs under.

viewType.description: The view type, from the documentation model's list of view types.

mermaid.description: The Mermaid source, without the code fence.

shows.description: The names of the elements the diagram shows.

SpecialistAnswer.description: A design specialist's or diagram author's answer to one request.

kind.description: The request's `kind`, as the request file states it. An answer to a `question` has no `decisions` and no `diagrams`; an answer to a `task` has both.

answer.description: The answer to the question in one sentence, or for a task what was decided in one sentence.

assumptions.description: What the answer rests on that the sources do not establish.

alternatives.description: The alternatives considered; empty unless the request asks for them.

decisions.description: For a task, the decisions as design facts; absent for a question.

diagrams.description: For a diagram task, the diagrams drawn; empty for any other task; absent for a question.

TrdChange.description: One change to the TRD. For `remove`, only `id` carries meaning and the other texts are empty.

id.description: The requirement id; for `add`, an empty string lets trd-author assign the next id.

statement.description: What must be true, with its checkable value.

appliesTo.description: The matrix id of the element.

HeadingCitation.description: One heading of an arc42 document: never a whole document.

source.description: The arc42 path relative to the architecture root.

heading.description: The heading as `atw-matrix node document:<path>` lists it.

TrdRequest.description: What the solutions architect asks of trd-author. The constraints that apply to the Epic are not listed here: trd-author reads them, with their statements and the headings they are stated in, from `atw-matrix epic <epic> --constraints`, the same command the architect reads them from.

epic.description: The Epic's beads id, which `atw-matrix epic` takes.

prdPath.description: The PRD file. trd-author reads the requirement headings `atw-matrix epic <epic>` names (each requirement's `name` is its PRD heading), not the whole file.

trdPath.description: The absolute path of the TRD file.

statePath.description: The absolute path of the architect's state file, whose `needs` name the PRD requirement headings each need comes from.

approvedHeadings.description: For `draft`, each effective arc42 heading that states a standing obligation the design relies on and that no constraint `atw-matrix epic <epic> --constraints` returns records; empty for `update`. A heading whose rules the matrix records as constraints is not listed: the command returns them.

sharedCapabilities.description: For `draft`, each shared capability the design uses, to be written as one requirement of kind `reuse`; empty for `update`.

changes.description: For `update`, the changes to apply; empty for `draft`.

answerPath.description: The absolute path the answer is written to.

NoSource.description: An obligation the PRD implies for which neither the PRD nor the approved material gives a source.

prdRequirement.description: The PRD requirement heading that implies it.

why.description: What the architecture would have to state for the obligation to have a source.

TrdRequirement.description: One technical requirement as the TRD states it. The script records it in the matrix as one constraint that points at it (the Epic and this id, a heading of the TRD) with where it is stated and what it applies to; its statement stays in the TRD.

id.description: The requirement id, as the TRD gives it: the text of the requirement's own heading in the TRD.

statement.description: What must be true, with its checkable value.

appliesTo.description: The matrix id of the entry the requirement applies to; an empty string when it applies to the Epic as a whole.

TrdAnswer.description: trd-author's answer to one request. The TRD itself is the file at the request's `trdPath`.

requirementIds.description: For `draft`, every requirement id in the TRD; for `update`, the ids added, changed and removed.

removed.description: For `update`, the ids of the requirements removed from the TRD; empty for `draft`.

requirements.description: Every requirement this answer's TRD write added or changed, exactly as the TRD now states it: for `draft`, every requirement the TRD states, one entry for each id in `requirementIds`; for `update`, each requirement added or changed. A removed requirement is named in `requirementIds` only. The script records the matrix's constraints, each a pointer to its requirement, from these entries and from no other file.

Restatement.description: A place that states a fact a second time, to be replaced by a link to the fact's home.

fact.description: The id of the fact in this request, or a short name for a fact an effective document states.

AppliedSettlement.description: A settled disagreement to apply to the documents.

disagreement.description: The matrix id of the disagreement entry.

corrections.description: Each place whose statement lost and is replaced by a link to the one that stands.

WriteRequest.description: What the solutions architect asks architecture-maintainer to write into arc42; one request where one can hold everything.

facts.description: Each fact with its statement and reason, its one home and the documents that must link to it.

restatements.description: Each place that restates a fact and is to be replaced by a link to its home.

diagrams.description: Each diagram a diagram author returned, to place under its home.

resultPath.description: The absolute path the write result is written to.

entry.description: The id of the fact, or a description of the restatement, settlement or diagram.

WriteResult.description: architecture-maintainer's result for one write request.

linksAdded.description: Each place a link to a home heading was added.

belowArchitectureLevel.description: Entries not written because they are below architecture level, for the architect to move to the TRD or to notesForSpecs.

notApplied.description: Entries that could not be applied for any other reason.

ScopeFinding.description: One defect in one unapproved item, measured against one criterion at the item's own level.

id.description: F1, F2 and so on, unique in the review.

criterion.description: The id of the criterion the item does not meet.

item.description: The item of the review scope: a document's matrix id or path, a document path and heading joined by `#`, or a TRD requirement id.

observation.description: What the item says or lacks, stated as a fact a reader can check.

correction.description: The bounded change that removes the defect.

doneWhen.description: The condition that shows the correction is made.

DependsOnApproved.description: An unapproved item that cannot be correct unless an approved statement is wrong.

AlternativeRequest.description: A request for a competing design of one item.

option.description: The option that was not considered.

why.description: Why it could plainly be better.

ScopeReview.description: One reviewer's result for the unapproved items its criteria apply to. Every item of its scope is in `passed` or has a finding, a `dependsOnApproved` report or an alternative request.

passed.description: The items that meet every criterion that applies to them.

RoutedItem.description: The lead's decision for one finding, alternative request or unsettled matter.

item.description: The finding id, the item of the alternative request, or the id of the unsettled matter.

raisedBy.description: The reviewer that raised it, or `aws-solutions-architect` for an unsettled matter.

steps.description: The ids of the journal steps the lead added for it; empty for `reject`.

LeadRouting.description: architecture-team-lead's output: one decision for each item it was started for.

requirements.description: The business requirements or section 2 constraints in conflict.

matter.description: The id of the matter in the question file.

stands.description: The id of the position that stands; an empty string only when an owner concern is raised.

reason.description: Why that position stands, from the evidence the two sides gave.

losingPositionChanges.description: What the losing position must change.

BuiltDifference.description: One difference, at architecture level, between code a Story built and the approved architecture.

element.description: The matrix id of the element.

code.description: Where the code shows it: repository, revision and file:line.

architecture.description: The approved arc42 heading it differs from.

difference.description: What the code does and what the architecture says, in one or two sentences.

document.description: The path, relative to the architecture root, of the built-difference document written for it.

BuiltComparison.description: built-architecture-comparer's result for one Story. An empty differences list means the code the Story built matches the approved architecture.
